title: On-delay and off-delay in Ladder: timers as blocks in a rung
summary: Place a TOF and a TON between a contact and a coil, and see that an off-delay keeps a light on after the button and an on-delay ignores a sensor that does not stay on.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show how a real sensor flickers or how a real lamp is wired.
objectives: Place a timer function block in a rung, with the contact feeding its IN and its output feeding the coil.
Tell an off-delay (TOF) from an on-delay (TON) by what each does when the input rises and falls.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/DelaysLd.ld.json two rungs connect a contact straight to a coil, so Light follows Button and Confirmed follows Sensor. Make Light stay ON for T#300ms after Button is released, and make Confirmed turn ON only after Sensor has stayed ON for T#200ms.
stages.checkpoint: You can say which of the two timers keeps an output on after its input falls, and which one waits before it turns its output on.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Button is pressed at {{t:100}} ms and released at {{t:300}} ms. Sensor is on from {{t:100}} to {{t:140}} ms, and again from {{t:500}} to {{t:900}} ms. Predict Light at {{t:450}} and {{t:650}} ms and Confirmed at {{t:450}} and {{t:800}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:DelaysLd.Light=true@450|ON}} at {{t:450}} ms, still inside the T#300ms hold; {{v:DelaysLd.Light=false@650|OFF}} at {{t:650}} ms; {{v:DelaysLd.Confirmed=false@450|OFF}} at {{t:450}} ms, because the pulse was too short; {{v:DelaysLd.Confirmed=true@800|ON}} at {{t:800}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program has no timers: Light drops the moment Button is released and Confirmed follows Sensor, so Light is OFF at {{t:450}} ms and Confirmed is ON at {{t:120}} ms. Change it so that Light stays ON until T#300ms after Button is released, and Confirmed turns ON only when Sensor has been ON for T#200ms without a break. Keep the contacts and the coils of both rungs.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named DelaysLd and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare Light at {{t:300}} and {{t:650}} ms with Confirmed at {{t:140}} and {{t:800}} ms: the TOF delays the fall of its input, the TON delays the rise.
stages.checkpoint: Light falls once, after the hold, and Confirmed rises once, after the sensor has stayed on for T#200ms; the short pulse at {{t:100}} ms never raises it.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Swap the two blocks, TON for the hold and TOF for the filter, and see which assertions fail. What does each block do to a short pulse?
stages.checkpoint: A TON ignores a pulse shorter than its preset and a TOF stretches a pulse by its preset, so in the swapped program the short sensor pulse gets through and is stretched, and Light waits before it turns on, falls as soon as Button is released, and never turns on if the press is shorter than the preset.

hints.text: The coil must not see the contact directly. Which block sits between them, and what does each of the two blocks do to a signal?
In the first rung place a TOF with PT T#300ms and in the second a TON with PT T#200ms, each between its contact and its coil, and leave IN connected to the contact.

faultCases: The starting program has no timers: Light drops the moment Button is released and Confirmed follows Sensor, so Light is OFF at {{t:450}} ms and Confirmed is ON at {{t:120}} ms.
